acceptance_checks: A registered task's locks equal its frozen plan's locks exactly — nothing is injected at registration, lock acquisition or worktree allocation.

MergeGate accepts a PR carrying the task's own mirror evidence with narrow product-path locks only, including a post-execution runner/EXEC record reached transitively through a check ledger's evidence array.
MergeGate still blocks a mirror file belonging to another task or another goal.
A task file listing a ledger that is not its own — foreign goal_id or task_id — does not expand the derived set, so a PR-authored task file cannot widen its own effective locks.
Frozen-plan matching compares locks exactly and rejects any difference, including path:.shiki/**.
validate_shiki no longer warns for a narrow-lock task on an active goal, and its advisory text no longer claims a dispatch-time .shiki lock guarantee.
non_goals: Exempting .shiki from files_outside_locks (ADR 0016 step B, needs R-02 first)
Changing the lock conflict algorithm or what the loop syncs

findings.detail: shiki_loop._evidence_relatives_for_task iterates ledger_evidence unconditionally and syncs every referenced .shiki path (including a completion ledger with task_id=null pointing at .shiki/reports/R-*.json). _derive_task_mirror_locks only expands ledgers whose goal_id AND task_id both match the task, so such a goal-scoped ledger's report/EXEC evidence is not covered by the derived set. This is harmless in this diff because it is additive and loop tasks still declare path:.shiki/** (which covers everything), and because the mismatch fails closed (blocks, never over-permits). But if the goal is to eventually drop the .shiki/** declaration and rely solely on the derived set, a task reaching closeout would have its completion report blocked. Worth confirming the closeout/completion PR path never relies on this derivation, or extending the derivation to goal-scoped ledgers listed in the task's own ledger_evidence.
findings.title: Derivation does not expand goal-scoped (task_id: null) ledgers that the loop syncs unconditionally

findings.detail: test_all_frozen_plan_tasks_cover_their_synced_evidence asserts checked >= 19, and the repo currently contains exactly ~19 tasks across its four spec-frozen plans (P-0001, b25b41ec, bac3fdc7, 1fa476be). The test passes today but is fragile: removing a task from any frozen plan would drop the count below 19 and fail the assertion. Consider deriving the threshold from the discovered plans rather than hard-coding it.
findings.title: FrozenPlanCorpusTests threshold (checked >= 19) is pinned to the current exact frozen-task count

scope: Give a task's declared locks mirror coverage WITHOUT writing anything into the stored locks. Remove injection from every write site in scripts/shiki_tasks.py: locks stay exactly what the plan declared. Instead, scripts/mergegate_check.py derives the task's mirror set at judgment time — from its task id, goal id and its ledger_evidence, including every .shiki-prefixed path those ledgers' evidence arrays reference — and unions it into the effective lock set passed to files_outside_locks. Deriving at read time is the point: the loop appends ledgers and writes runner/EXEC records AFTER dispatch (ten append_ledger sites in shiki_loop.py, none of which re-inject), so any scheme that writes coverage into stored locks is already stale by the time MergeGate reads it. Bound the derivation so it cannot be widened by a PR-authored task file: expand only ledgers listed in the task's own ledger_evidence whose goal_id and task_id match the task, and ignore any other reference. Frozen-plan matching then compares locks exactly, with no injected-set tolerance, because nothing is injected. Finally, correct the locks_cover_shiki_state advisory in scripts/validate_shiki.py, whose message asserts a dispatch-time path:.shiki/** guarantee that no longer exists and would otherwise warn on every task registered under the new model.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Inject id-scoped mirror locks at task registration
